transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aman (Kepler Head of ML), Sofia (Kepler DevOps), Liam (CTO)

Summary (auto): quickstart path, credits, security review, pilot/benchmark steps discussed.

00:00 Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining, can folks introduce themselves quickly?
00:07 Aman: yeah Aman here, head of ML at Kepler, we own the assistant project, thanks for doing this
00:11 Sofia: Sofia, infra/devops, I'll care about VPC and data retention stuff
00:15 Liam: Liam, CTO, mostly listening for procurement and security questions
00:20 Maya: great, quick agenda - quickstart and free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated/private, security and next steps
00:35 Diego: just to set expectations, we'll walk through the self-serve API, show how to get first tokens in minutes, then talk about Dedicated and Private if you need isolation
01:02 Aman: our main goal is a customer-facing assistant that needs sub-second-ish latency for short prompts and P95 < 700ms if possible, but cost matters a lot since traffic could be large
01:18 Diego: ok that tracks, for PLG quickstart the hosted Redwood API is fastest to get going - you sign up, get free credits, create an API key, quickstart runs in under 10 minutes usually. Time-to-first-token is mostly SDK setup + sample prompt
01:35 Maya: the free credits are intended to let you prototype and run small benchmarks; we can also provision a short dedicated pilot if you want capacity guarantees later
01:50 Sofia: question - on hosted, what are the data retention and encryption guarantees? we need to know about KMS and audit logs, and whether we can disable logging to keep PII off the control plane
02:07 Maya: good question. Redwood hosted supports customer-controlled KMS for Private, for hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit, we offer SOC2 and ISO certs, and we have audit logs. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; we'll send the SOC2 report after this call
02:29 Liam: is there an option for a VPC peering for hosted? or is that only Private?
02:36 Diego: VPC peering is part of Redwood Private, dedicated has network controls but not full VPC peering to our control plane. If you need customer-managed networking and on-prem options, Private is the route; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput but still managed infra
02:57 Aman: how about latency and model variants - can we fallback to smaller models during peak to keep latency low?
03:06 Diego: yes, smart routing supports model variants and fallback policies; you can pin a model and have automatic fallback to a quantized variant if capacity is constrained. Also batching and prefix cache reduces per-token cost but we can tune to preserve latency SLOs
03:25 Aman: nice, we probably want a mix - hosted for dev/early PLG, then Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for enterprise customers with data residency needs
03:39 Sofia: what about SSO/SSO provisioning and RBAC for the console? 
03:44 Maya: SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported, roles and RBAC in the Console, plus audit logs; we'll include details in the security pack
04:01 Liam: procurement question - what's the typical path from free credits to a paid Dedicated commit? any minimums?
04:11 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; no lock-in for hosted usage, but Dedicated usually involves a minimum monthly commit depending on GPU footprint. We'll share a pricing/commitment template. For many customers we start with hosted, then move to Dedicated when traffic is predictable
04:31 Aman: for the benchmark we want to compare 1) hosted Redwood with model X, 2) Dedicated quantized variant, 3) baseline current infra (we use SageMaker for fine-tuned models) - can you help run that?
04:47 Diego: absolutely, we can provide a benchmark script and run an onboarding bench with your sample dataset. For hosted it's straightforward; for Dedicated we'll coordinate with capacity scheduling
05:02 Sofia: any gotchas around KV cache and long context length? some of our prompts use ~8k tokens for multi-turn history
05:12 Diego: our runtime supports KV cache management and attention optimizations; long contexts are ok but cost and latency tradeoffs apply. We'll recommend quantization for Dedicated and tuning for sequence length distribution
05:30 Aman: ok great. can you also confirm logging: we need to ensure PII isn't stored in control plane logs from hosted envs
05:38 Maya: yes, we'll include the exact retention defaults and options; for PII-sensitive workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with log forwarding and selective redaction
05:50 Liam: what's the onboarding time for Private?
05:54 Diego: Private (VPC/on-prem) usually takes longer - a few weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup; Dedicated is faster but still requires capacity provisioning. Hosted is minutes to hours for basic access
06:10 Aman: estimate cost per 1k tokens for the models you recommend? we need ballpark numbers for budgeting
06:16 Maya: we'll send pricing ranges; Redwood Optimize also gives suggestions for batching/quantization to reduce per-token cost - we'll include a sample report after the bench
06:30 Sofia: are there existing customers in regulated industries you can point to? e.g. healthcare/fintech
06:35 Maya: yes, a number of enterprise customers use Dedicated/Private for regulated use cases; we'll include anonymized references and case studies
06:45 Aman: ok next steps recap?
06:50 Maya: send SOC2/ISO and security whitepaper, share quickstart guide + free credits promo, Diego to prepare benchmark script and schedule a 30-min bench session, Kepler to provide sample dataset and success criteria. We'll aim to have the bench scheduled next week
07:10 Liam: sounds good, thanks everyone
07:15 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and docs
